claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I do have a child I'm responsible for. I have one child - my son Alex, who's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

Now I need to ask: **Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. We're based in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you! Now I need to understand your living situation with Alex.

**Does Alex live with you, or do you have a different arrangement?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to check a few more things to complete the eligibility assessment.

**Has anyone else already claimed Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, the other parent or another family member?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Just a couple more questions to ensure I have all the information needed.

**Are you or your partner (if you have one) a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, pre-settled status, or another immigration status that I should know about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a UK citizen, so no immigration issues there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! One final question to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex in any special circumstances, such as being in hospital, care, or residential accommodation for an extended period, or does he live away from home for any reason?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he was in local authority care for a bit - just a couple of months earlier this year - but he's back home with me now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that. I need to understand this situation a bit better.

**When exactly did Alex return home to live with you? And does he now live with you full-time, or does he still spend time in care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been back home with me full-time now. That was earlier this year - he was only in care for about 8 weeks total, and now he's living with me permanently again.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Based on all the information you've provided, I now have enough to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Let me review your situation:

- You have one child, Alex, aged 8
- You live in the UK (Manchester)
- Alex lives with you full-time now
- You're a UK citizen
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- Alex was in local authority care for about 8 weeks earlier this year but is now back home with you permanently

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why you qualify:

✅ **Alex meets the age requirement** - He's 8 years old (under 16)
✅ **You live in the UK** - You're based in Manchester
✅ **You're a UK citizen** - No immigration restrictions
✅ **Alex lives with you** - He's back home with you full-time
✅ **You're responsible for Alex** - He's living in your care
✅ **No one else is claiming** - Nobody else has claimed Child Benefit for him

The fact that Alex was in local authority care for about 8 weeks earlier this year doesn't affect your current eligibility, since he's now back home with you permanently.

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit. If you haven't already applied, you should do so to start receiving payments. Remember that only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child, so as long as no one else claims for Alex, you should be fine.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
